A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FusionRoute and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–C. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendix examples can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, GPT-4o preference comparisons, complementary-logit and training ablations, and qualitative routing examples.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results in Tables 1–2, Figures 3–4, and Appendix C.2.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same token-level expert selection, complementary logit addition, disagreement-based SFT routing loss, CDPO, and mixed training procedure. Section 3.2.2 presents the existing CDPO objective more compactly without establishing an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both retain PerfectBlend and OpenHermes training data and evaluation on GSM8K, MATH500, MBPP, HumanEval, IFEval, and held-out PerfectBlend prompts. No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the same experts, Sequence Selection, Collab, DARE, TaskArithmetic, and fine-tuned baseline. Comparator membership in the routing and CDPO ablations is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Model checkpoints, training budgets, greedy decoding, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged. Both retain the 500-prompt GPT-4o comparison and Appendix C.1's evaluation sample counts, token limits, and judging prompt.

E4.justification: Sections 6.1–6.2 retain the same complementary-logit and CDPO ablations. The model-scale analysis and all four qualitative routing examples in Appendix C.2 are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The point-estimate reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 contain identical results, including FusionRoute's average accuracies of 0.566 for Llama-3 and 0.426 for Gemma-2. Figures 3–4 use identical plot images, and the appendix responses and reported qualitative findings are retained.

T1.justification: Section 4.3.1 explicitly adds the condition that each selected fused expert minimizes total variation distance to the optimal policy. Its value bound now stops at T Q_max Delta, removing v1's additional R_max T Delta bound. The impossibility theorem and Appendix A–B arguments remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about complementary token-level routing, limitations of expert-only collaboration, efficiency, and empirical advantages.

C2.justification: Section 4.3.1 makes the selection condition underlying the complementary-policy guarantee explicit. Section 5.1 also changes the interpretation of the unchanged fine-tuning comparison: v1 describes isolating collaboration and complementary logits, while v2 describes isolating complementary logits alone.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix C retain the same checkpoint identifiers, initialization, hyperparameters, training sample counts, generation settings, and evaluation prompt. Project and data access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography is identical. The introduction, related-work sections, and Appendix B retain the same positioning against Collab, CO-LLM, model merging, MoE, and other cited approaches.

P1.justification: Several preliminaries, method, and experimental-setup paragraphs are shortened or rewritten. The performance difference lemma moves earlier within Section 4.2, while overall section and appendix organization remains intact. The rewrite introduces inconsistent CDPO shorthand and a duplicated mixed-domain evaluation sentence.

P2.justification: Figure 1 expands from an introductory inset to a standalone page. Figures 2–4 and Algorithm 1 are repositioned, with Figure 4 now accompanying Section 6.2. Several equations become inline or more compact; figure content and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The explicit selection condition and removal of the unexplained R_max-based simplification in Section 4.3.1 modestly improve theoretical precision. Figure 1 is more legible, and Figure 4 better accompanies its discussion. These limited gains outweigh small editing regressions, including inconsistent CDPO shorthand and an overly narrow interpretation of the fine-tuning comparison. Experimental evidence and appendix proofs remain unchanged.
